summary: Initializes a buffered I/O context with a 4096-byte heap buffer (via MallocWrapperForNhMalloc) and falls back to a 2-byte inline storage area when the allocation fails. Sets the cursor, the remaining-byte count to 0, the buffer base, the capacity (4096 heap / 2 inline), and a flags field distinguishing the two backing modes (heap bit 3, inline bit 2). Increments a global file-open counter on entry. Used by six file/stream handling callers.

local_names.this: buffer context object (5 dwords of inline storage start at this + 5 dwords)

operations.description: Increment the global file-open counter dword_8D3EC8 on entry.
Call MallocWrapperForNhMalloc(4096) and store the returned heap pointer at this+8 (buffer base).
If the allocation returned non-null: OR bit 3 into the flags field at this+0xC and set the capacity field at this+0x18 to 4096.
Else (allocation failed): OR bit 2 into the flags field at this+0xC, set the buffer base to the inline area (a1 + 5 dwords) and the capacity field at this+0x18 to 2.
Zero the remaining-byte count at this+4 and store the chosen buffer base into the cursor pointer at this+0.

unresolved: Meaning of the flag bits (bit 3 heap-backed, bit 2 inline-backed) is DERIVED from the two branches; the exact flag enum is not in the packet.
Semantics of the capacity field at this+0x18 (total bytes vs units) is inferred from context, not proven.
Identity and struct layout of the buffer context type are unknown; callers are file/stream handlers but the owning class is not established.
